text:
lina: RFC follow-up — proposal to extract continuous-batcher into its own service and own scheduler. thinking this will let us apply per-tenant QoS without touching runtime hot path. links: https://rfc/internal/continuous-batcher-extract :eyes:

adam: +1 to extraction, but worried about extra RPC hop on hot path. Have numbers on added p99?

marta: we measured a 0.8–1.5ms added hop on gRPC within region last week. that kills nothing but matters for sub-10ms SLOs.

joel: if we co-locate the batcher sidecar on same host (unix socket) we can shave that down. tradeoff is ops complexity + coupling.

lina: agreed — options: 1) sidecar per runtime-worker (low latency, higher memory/ops), 2) colocated process pool on host, 3) remote service with fast rpc and fallback. we should list pros/cons and operational cost.

adam: + list of concrete concerns: cache locality (kv cache must remain local to runtime to avoid cache misses), backpressure propagation, and rollover on tenant spikes.

marta: exactly. if the batcher takes batching decisions without access to the runtime's KV prefix cache, quality regressions can happen. we might need a light-weight cache-proxy API.

joel: proposal sketch in config form:
```
continuous_batcher.enabled = true
continuous_batcher.mode = "sidecar"  # sidecar | colocated | rpc
continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens = 2048
continuous_batcher.per_tenant_scheduler = true
continuous_batcher.cache_proxy_addr = "/run/cache-proxy.sock"
```

lina: technical constraints we should confirm before choosing: a) binding to existing socket model across cloud providers, b) mTLS for RPC if remote, c) CPU isolation for sidecars, d) autoscale granularity.

adam: ops note: sidecars multiply process count per GPU node. our current node image tests for 6 processes; we need CI perf runs for 12 and 24 before approving.

marta: also: rollout plan — start with colocated pool for non-latency-critical workloads (embeddings/rerank) then canary sidecar on a subset of clients. that reduces blast radius. :thumbsup:

joel: what about fairness? per-tenant scheduler needs token-level accounting and leak-bucket semantics. keeping it inside batcher service means we replicate accounting state — either stream from control-plane or keep it local with periodic reconciliation. both have tradeoffs.

lina: decision reqs: 1) where KV cache lives (runtime vs shared proxy), 2) initial deployment model (colocated pool -> sidecar), 3) accounting model (stream vs local recon), 4) rollout gating (perf + quality evals).

adam: i'm going to sketch a quick perf gating checklist and add to RFC: perf microbench (p99 delta), quality eval promptset (LLamaBench-ish), rollout checklist, CI node-count expansion, infra cost delta.

marta: I'll prototype a cache-proxy shim that exposes: `GET /prefix/:key` and a cheap hint API `POST /prefetch` to avoid large KV churn. will attach prototype logs.

joel: ops-bot note: deploy window for experiments is mon-tue 02:00-06:00 UTC. schedule test canary then.

lina: nice. next action items: @adam write perf gating PR, @marta prototype cache-proxy and run small-scale perf, @joel evaluate sidecar image changes and CI node-tests. I'll update RFC with chosen sequence.

ops-bot: Reaction added :white_check_mark: to lina's message.

marta: tiny thing — if we go sidecar we must add ruche health checks so kube doesn't evict because of transient CPU bursts. put that in the rollout checklist.

adam: also we should flag billing/metrics: batcher should emit per-tenant token counts with an open access metric so billing team can verify cost changes.

lina: good call. I'll cc billing and add a metric contract section.

joel: ok let's reconvene after prototypes. short sync next wed 09:30 PT?

lina: booked. thanks everyone.
